subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let AB = 2î + 4ĵ − 5k̂ and AD = î + 2ĵ + λk̂, λ ∈ R. Let the projection of the vector v = î + ĵ + k̂ on the diagonal AC of the parallelogram ABCD be of length one unit. If α, β (α > β) are the roots of the equation λ²x² − 6λx + 5 = 0, then 2α − β is equal to:
explanation: AC = AB + AD = 3î + 6ĵ + (λ − 5)k̂. The projection of v on AC has length |v·AC|/|AC| = |4 + λ|/√(45 + (λ − 5)²) = 1, giving (λ + 4)² = 45 + (λ − 5)² ⇒ λ = 3. The quadratic becomes 9x² − 18x + 5 = 0 with roots α = 5/3 and β = 1/3, so 2α − β = 10/3 − 1/3 = 3.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let the relation R on the set M = {1, 2, 3, …, 16} be given by R = {(x, y) : 4y = 5x − 3, x, y ∈ M}. Then the minimum number of elements required to be added in R, in order to make the relation symmetric, is equal to:
explanation: From 4y = 5x − 3, the pairs in M are (3, 3), (7, 8) and (11, 13). To make R symmetric, the reverse pairs (8, 7) and (13, 11) must be added, so 2 elements.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let the line x = −1 divide the area of the region {(x, y) : 1 + x² ≤ y ≤ 3 − x} in the ratio m : n, where gcd(m, n) = 1. Then m + n is equal to:
explanation: The curves y = 1 + x² and y = 3 − x meet at x = −2 and x = 1. The region cut by the line x = −1 is divided into areas in the ratio 20 : 7, so m = 20, n = 7 and m + n = 27.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Two distinct numbers a and b are selected at random from 1, 2, 3, …, 50. The probability that their product ab is divisible by 3 is:
explanation: Among 1, 2, …, 50 there are 34 numbers not divisible by 3 and 16 divisible by 3. P = 1 − C(34,2)/C(50,2) = 1 − 561/1225 = 664/1225.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let f(x) = x²⁰²⁵ − x²⁰⁰⁰, x ∈ [0, 1], and let the minimum value of the function f(x) in the interval [0, 1] be 80⁸⁰ · n⁻⁸¹. Then n is equal to:
explanation: f′(x) = x¹⁹⁹⁹(2025x²⁵ − 2000). The critical point is x = (2000/2025)^(1/25) = (80/81)^(1/25), where f attains its minimum value f_min = (80/81)⁸⁰ · (−1/81) = −80⁸⁰ · 81⁻⁸¹, so n = −81.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let P(α, β, γ) be the point on the line (x − 1)/2 = (y + 1)/(−3) = z at a distance 4√14 from the point (1, −1, 0) and nearer to the origin. Then the shortest distance between the lines (x − α)/1 = (y − β)/2 = (z − γ)/3 and (x + 5)/2 = (y − 10)/1 = (z − 3)/1 is equal to:
explanation: Points on the given line are (1 + 2t, −1 − 3t, t). Distance √14|t| = 4√14 gives t = ±4; nearer to the origin gives t = −4, so P(−7, 11, −4). For the two lines with direction vectors b₁ = (1,2,3) and b₂ = (2,1,1), the shortest distance is |(a₂ − a₁)·(b₁×b₂)|/|b₁×b₂| = 28/√35 = 4√7/√5.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If a random variable X has the probability distribution [X: 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; P(X): 0, 2k, k, 3k, 2k², 2k, k + k², 7k²], then P(3 < X ≤ 6) is equal to:

subject: Mathematics
question_text: The number of distinct real solutions of the equation x|x + 4| + 3|x + 2| + 10 = 0 is:
explanation: For x < −4 the equation reduces to x² + 7x − 4 = 0, which has one acceptable root (√65 − 7)/2. For −4 ≤ x < −2 and x ≥ −2 the quadratics x² + x + 4 = 0 and x² + 7x + 16 = 0 have negative discriminants. Hence there is exactly 1 distinct real solution.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let f : [1, ∞) → R be a differentiable function. If 6∫₁ˣ f(t) dt = 3x f(x) + x³ − 4 for all x ≥ 1, then the value of f(2) − f(3) is:
explanation: Differentiating both sides: 6f(x) = 3xf′(x) + 3f(x) + 3x² ⇒ x f′(x) = f(x) + x² ⇒ f′(x) = f(x)/x + x. Solving gives f(x) = −x² + 2x (using f(1) = 1). Hence f(2) = 0, f(3) = −3, so f(2) − f(3) = 3.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If the line ax + 2y = 1, where a ∈ R, does not meet the hyperbola x² − 9y² = 9, then a possible value of a is:
explanation: Substituting y = (1 − ax)/2 into x² − 9y² = 9 gives (4 − 9a²)x² + 18ax − 45 = 0. For no intersection the discriminant must be negative: 720 − 1296a² < 0 ⇒ a² > 5/9 ⇒ |a| > 0.745. Among the options only a = 0.8 works.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If the image of the point P(1, 2, a) in the line (x − 6)/3 = (y − 7)/2 = (7 − z)/2 is Q(5, b, c), then a² + b² + c² is equal to:
explanation: The midpoint M of PQ lies on the line and PQ is perpendicular to it. Solving gives b = 8, c + a = 18 and c + a = 12 → c = 15, a = 3. Hence a² + b² + c² = 9 + 64 + 225 = 298.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let the set of all values of r, for which the circles (x + 1)² + (y + 4)² = r² and x² + y² − 4x − 2y − 4 = 0 intersect at two distinct points, be the interval (α, β). Then αβ is equal to:
explanation: The second circle has centre (2, 1) and radius 3; the first has centre (−1, −4) and radius r. The distance between the centres is √34. For two intersection points, |r − 3| < √34 < r + 3, giving r ∈ (√34 − 3, √34 + 3). Hence αβ = (√34 − 3)(√34 + 3) = 34 − 9 = 25.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If A = [[2,3],[3,5]], then the determinant of the matrix (A²⁰²⁵ − 3A²⁰²⁴ + A²⁰²³) is:
explanation: A²⁰²⁵ − 3A²⁰²⁴ + A²⁰²³ = A²⁰²³(A² − 3A + I). Now A² = [[13,21],[21,34]], so A² − 3A + I = [[8,12],[12,20]] with determinant 8·20 − 12·12 = 16. Since det(A) = 1, det of the whole expression = 1²⁰²³ · 16 = 16.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If the domain of the function f(x) = sin⁻¹((5 − x)/(3 + 2x)) + 1/logₑ(10 − x) is (−∞, α] ∪ [β, γ) − {δ}, then 6(α + β + γ + δ) is equal to:

subject: Mathematics
question_text: The value of ∫(from −π/2 to π/2) 1/([x] + 4) dx, where [·] denotes the greatest integer function, is:
explanation: Split the interval where [x] is constant: on [−π/2,−1] it equals 1/2, on [−1,0) it is 1/3, on [0,1) it is 1/4 and on [1,π/2] it is 1/5. The integral = (π/2 − 1)/2 + 1/3 + 1/4 + (π/2 − 1)/5 = 7(3π − 1)/60.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: The coefficient of x⁴⁸ in (1 + x) + 2(1 + x)² + 3(1 + x)³ + … + 100(1 + x)¹⁰⁰ is equal to:

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If the chord joining the points P₁(x₁, y₁) and P₂(x₂, y₂) on the parabola y² = 12x subtends a right angle at the vertex of the parabola, then x₁x₂ − y₁y₂ is equal to:
explanation: Parametric points on y² = 12x are (3t², 6t). A chord subtends a right angle at the vertex when t₁t₂ = −4. Then x₁x₂ − y₁y₂ = 9(t₁t₂)² − 36t₁t₂ = 9(16) − 36(−4) = 144 + 144 = 288.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: The number of solutions of tan⁻¹(4x) + tan⁻¹(6x) = π/6, where −1/(2√6) < x < 1/(2√6), is equal to:
explanation: Using tan(A + B) = (tan A + tan B)/(1 − tan A tan B), (4x + 6x)/(1 − 24x²) = 1/√3 ⇒ 24x² + 10√3 x − 1 = 0, which has exactly one root lying in the given interval. Hence there is 1 solution.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let the solution curve of the differential equation x dy − y dx = √(x² + y²) dx, x > 0, y(1) = 0, be y = y(x). Then y(3) is equal to:
explanation: Dividing by x dx, dy/dx = y/x + √(1 + (y/x)²). With y = ux this gives u + √(1 + u²) = kx, and y(1) = 0 gives k = 1. At x = 3, y + √(9 + y²) = 9 ⇒ y = 4.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If the sum of the first four terms of an A.P. is 6 and the sum of its first six terms is 4, then the sum of its first twelve terms is:

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let A be a 3 × 3 matrix such that A + Aᵀ = O. If A[[1],[−1],[0]] = [[3],[3],[2]], A²[[1],[−1],[0]] = [[−3],[19],[−24]] and det(adj(2adj(A + I))) = 2^α · 3^β · 11^γ, where α, β, γ are non-negative integers, then the value of α + β + γ is:

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let α = (−1 + i√3)/2 and β = (−1 − i√3)/2, where i = √(−1). If (7 − 7α + 9β)²⁰ + (9 + 7α − 7β)²⁰ + (−7 + 9α + 7β)²⁰ + (14 + 7α + 7β)²⁰ = m¹⁰, then the value of m is:
explanation: α and β are the non-real cube roots of unity, so α + β = −1, αβ = 1 and 1 + α + β = 0. Simplifying each 20th-power term (using the periodicity of powers of the cube roots) reduces the sum to 49¹⁰, hence m = 49.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If ∫ (sin x)^(−11/2) (cos x)^(−5/2) dx = −(p₁/q₁)(cot x)^(9/2) − (p₂/q₂)(cot x)^(5/2) − (p₃/q₃)(cot x)^(1/2) + (p₄/q₄)(cot x)^(−3/2) + C, where pᵢ, qᵢ are positive integers with gcd(pᵢ, qᵢ) = 1 for i = 1, 2, 3, 4, then the value of 15p₁p₂p₃p₄/(q₁q₂q₃q₄) is:
explanation: Write the integrand as (tan x)^(−1/2) sec⁶x and put t = tan x. Integrating gives p₁ = 2, p₂ = 6, p₃ = 6, p₄ = 2 and q₁ = 9, q₂ = 5, q₃ = 1, q₄ = 3. Hence 15·2·6·6·2/(9·5·1·3) = 2160/135 = 16.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: If (cos²48° − sin²12°)/(sin²24° − sin²6°) = (α + β√5)/2, where α, β ∈ N, then the value of α + β is:
explanation: Using sin(A + B)sin(A − B) = sin²A − sin²B and cos(A + B)cos(A − B) = cos²A − sin²B, the ratio becomes cos60°cos36°/(sin30°sin18°) = (3 + √5)/2, so α = 3, β = 1 and α + β = 4.

subject: Mathematics
question_text: Let ABC be a triangle. Consider four points P₁, P₂, P₃, P₄ on the side AB, five points P₅, …, P₉ on the side BC, and four points P₁₀, …, P₁₃ on the side AC. None of these points is a vertex of triangle ABC. Then the total number of pentagons that can be formed by taking all the vertices from the points P₁, P₂, …, P₁₃ is:
explanation: A pentagon cannot use three collinear vertices. Case 1 (2 from AB, 2 from BC, 1 from AC): C(4,2)·C(5,2)·4 = 240. Case 2 (2 from AB, 1 from BC, 2 from AC): C(4,2)·5·C(4,2) = 180. Case 3 (1 from AB, 2 from BC, 2 from AC): 4·C(5,2)·C(4,2) = 240. Total = 240 + 180 + 240 = 660.

subject: Physics
question_text: A solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 10 cm is kept in contact with another solid sphere of mass 10 kg and radius 20 cm. The moment of inertia of this pair of spheres about the tangent passing through the point of contact is ___ kg·m².

subject: Physics
question_text: A 7.9 MeV α-particle scatters from a target material of atomic number 79. From the given data, the estimated diameter of the nuclei of the target material is (approximately) ___ m.
explanation: At the closest distance of approach, kinetic energy equals electrostatic potential energy: r = k(2e)(79e)/E = 9×10⁹·2·(1.6×10⁻¹⁹)²·79/(7.9×10⁶·1.6×10⁻¹⁹) = 2.88×10⁻¹⁴ m. The diameter is D = 2r = 5.76×10⁻¹⁴ m.

subject: Physics
question_text: Six point charges are kept 60° apart from each other on the circumference of a circle of radius R as shown in the figure. The net electric field at the centre of the circle is: (ε₀ is the permittivity of free space)
explanation: Each charge contributes a field of magnitude E = kQ/R². Resolving the six fields along the given 60° arrangement and superposing, the net field at the centre is Q/(4πε₀R²)(√3î − ĵ).

subject: Physics
question_text: XPQY is a vertical smooth long loop having a total resistance R, where PX is parallel to QY and the separation between them is l. A constant magnetic field B perpendicular to the plane of the loop exists in the entire space. A rod CD of length L (L > l) and mass m is made to slide down from rest under gravity as shown in the figure. The terminal speed acquired by the rod is ___ m/s.
explanation: At terminal speed the magnetic force balances gravity: mg = BIl = B(Bvl/R)l = B²vl²/R, so v = mgR/(B²l²).

subject: Physics
question_text: The escape velocity from a spherical planet A is 10 km/s. The escape velocity from another planet B, whose density and radius are 10% of those of planet A, is ___ m/s.

subject: Physics
question_text: A meter bridge with two resistances R₁ and R₂ as shown in figure was balanced (null point) at 40 cm from the point P. The null point changed to 50 cm from the point P, when a 16 Ω resistance is connected in parallel to R₂. The values of resistances R₁ and R₂ are:
explanation: Balanced bridge: R₁/R₂ = 40/60 = 2/3. After putting 16 Ω in parallel with R₂, the effective R₂′ = 16R₂/(16 + R₂) and R₁/R₂′ = 50/50 = 1. Solving gives R₂ = 8 Ω and R₁ = 16/3 Ω.

subject: Physics
question_text: A projectile is thrown upward at an angle 60° with the horizontal. The speed of the projectile is 20 m/s when its direction of motion is 45° with the horizontal. The initial speed of the projectile is ___ m/s.
explanation: The horizontal component of velocity is constant: u cos60° = 20 cos45°, i.e. u/2 = 20/√2, giving u = 20√2 m/s.

subject: Physics
question_text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Pressure of a fluid is exerted only on a solid surface in contact as the fluid-pressure does not exist everywhere in a still fluid. Statement II: Excess potential energy of the molecules on the surface of a liquid, when compared to the interior, results in surface tension. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.1: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.4: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

explanation: By Pascal's law, pressure exists at every point in a still fluid, not just at boundaries, so Statement I is false. The excess surface potential energy compared with the interior gives rise to surface tension, so Statement II is true.

subject: Physics
question_text: Find the correct combination of A, B, C and D inputs which can cause the LED to glow.
explanation: The LED glows only when it is forward biased (higher potential at P, lower at Q). Analysing the logic gate circuit, the input combination 1101 produces the required levels for the LED to conduct.

subject: Physics
question_text: Net gravitational force at the centre of a square is found to be F₁ when four particles having masses M, 2M, 3M and 4M are placed at the four corners of the square as shown in figure, and it is F₂ when the positions of 3M and 4M are interchanged. The ratio F₁/F₂ = α/√5. The value of α is:
explanation: The fields of the masses at equal distances from the centre superpose to give F₁ = 2√2·(GMm₀/a²) and F₂ = √10·(GMm₀/a²). Hence F₁/F₂ = 2√2/√10 = 2/√5, so α = 2.

subject: Physics
question_text: The minimum frequency of photon required to break a particle of mass 15.348 amu into 4 α-particles is ___ kHz. [Mass of He nucleus = 4.002 amu, 1 amu = 1.66×10⁻²⁷ kg, h = 6.6×10⁻³⁴ J·s and c = 3×10⁸ m/s]

subject: Physics
question_text: A cylindrical tube AB of length l, closed at both ends, contains an ideal gas of 1 mol having molecular weight M. The tube is rotated in a horizontal plane with constant angular velocity ω about an axis perpendicular to AB and passing through the edge at end A, as shown in the figure. If P_A and P_B are the pressures at A and B respectively, then (consider the temperature to be the same at all points in the tube):
explanation: Integrating dP = ρω²x dx with ρ = PM/RT from x = 0 to x = l gives ln(P_B/P_A) = Mω²l²/2RT, so P_B = P_A exp(Mω²l²/2RT).

subject: Physics
question_text: Rods x and y of equal dimensions but of different materials are joined as shown in figure. Temperatures of end points A and F are maintained at 100°C and 40°C respectively. Given the thermal conductivity of rod x is three times that of rod y, the temperature at junction points B and E are (close to):
explanation: Applying the steady-state conduction equation H = kAΔT/L with the 3:1 conductivity ratio and equal dimensions, the junction temperatures work out to 89°C at B and 73°C at E.

subject: Physics
question_text: A thin convex lens of focal length 5 cm and a thin concave lens of focal length 4 cm are combined together (without any gap), and this combination has magnification m₁ when an object is placed 10 cm before the convex lens. Keeping the positions of the convex lens and object undisturbed, a gap of 1 cm is introduced between the lenses by moving the concave lens away, which leads to a change in magnification of the total lens system to m₂. The value of m₁/m₂ is:
explanation: This question was dropped by NTA (full marks awarded to all candidates). Intended solution: 1/F = 1/5 + 1/(−4) = −1/20, so F = −20 cm and m₁ = 2/3. With the 1 cm gap, m₂ = 4/13, so m₁/m₂ = (2/3)/(4/13) = 13/6.

subject: Physics
question_text: Consider an equilateral prism (refractive index √2). A ray of light is incident on its one surface at a certain angle i. If the emergent ray is found to graze along the other surface, then the angle of refraction at the incident surface is close to:
explanation: The prism angle A = 60°. For grazing emergence, the ray meets the second surface at the critical angle, giving r₂ = 45°. Then r₁ = A − r₂ = 60° − 45° = 15°.

subject: Physics
question_text: The volume of an ideal gas increases 8 times and temperature becomes (1/4)th of initial temperature during a reversible change. If there is no exchange of heat in this process (ΔQ = 0), then identify the gas from the following options (assuming the gases given in the options are ideal gases):
explanation: For an adiabatic change TV^(γ−1) = constant, so (1/4) = 8^(γ−1) ⇒ γ − 1 = 2/3 ⇒ γ = 5/3, the ratio for a monoatomic gas. Hence the gas is He.

subject: Physics
question_text: Electric field in a region is given by E = Ax î + By ĵ, where A = 10 V/m² and B = 5 V/m². If the electric potential at a point (10, 20) is 500 V, then the electric potential at origin is ___ V.
explanation: V_O − V = ∫E·dr = ∫₀¹⁰ 10x dx + ∫₀²⁰ 5y dy = 5x²|₀¹⁰ + (5/2)y²|₀²⁰ = 500 + 1000 = 1500. Hence V_O = 500 + 1500 = 2000 V.

subject: Physics
question_text: A simple pendulum has a bob with mass m and charge q. The pendulum string has negligible mass. When a uniform and horizontal electric field E is applied, the tension in the string changes. The final tension in the string, when the pendulum attains an equilibrium position is: (g: acceleration due to gravity)
explanation: At equilibrium the string is inclined so that the resultant of the gravitational force mg and the electric force qE is balanced by the tension: T = √((mg)² + (qE)²).

subject: Physics
question_text: Match the LIST-I with LIST-II: A. Spring constant → I. ML²T⁻²K⁻¹; B. Thermal conductivity → II. ML⁰T⁻²; C. Boltzmann constant → III. ML²T⁻³A⁻²; D. Inductive reactance → IV. MLT⁻³K⁻¹. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: Spring constant k = F/x has dimensions MLT⁻²/L = ML⁰T⁻² (II). Thermal conductivity has MLT⁻³K⁻¹ (IV). Boltzmann constant has ML²T⁻²K⁻¹ (I). Inductive reactance has ML²T⁻³A⁻² (III). So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

subject: Physics
question_text: Three identical coils C₁, C₂ and C₃ are closely placed such that they share a common axis. C₂ is exactly midway. C₁ carries current I in anti-clockwise direction while C₃ carries current I in clockwise direction. An induced current flows through C₂ will be in clockwise direction when:

options.1: C₁ and C₃ move with equal speeds away from C₂
options.2: C₁ moves away from C₂ and C₃ moves towards C₂
options.3: C₁ moves towards C₂ and C₃ moves away from C₂
options.4: C₁ and C₃ move with equal speeds towards C₂

explanation: By Lenz's law the induced current opposes the change of flux. When C₁ moves away and C₃ moves towards C₂, the changing flux through C₂ is such that the induced current in C₂ is clockwise.

subject: Physics
question_text: Two loudspeakers (L₁ and L₂) are placed with a separation of 10 m, as shown in the figure. Both speakers are fed with an audio input signal of the same frequency with constant volume. A voice recorder, initially at point A, at equidistance to both loudspeakers, is moved by 25 m along the line AB while monitoring the audio signal. The measured signal was found to undergo 10 cycles of minima and maxima during the movement. The frequency of the input signal is ___ Hz. (Speed of sound in air is 324 m/s and √5 = 2.23)
explanation: The path difference changes from 0 to (50 − 44.6) = 5.4 m over 10 fringes, so λ = 5.4/10 = 0.54 m. Hence f = v/λ = 324/0.54 = 600 Hz.

subject: Physics
question_text: The electric field of a plane electromagnetic wave, travelling in an unknown non-magnetic medium is given by E_y = 20 sin(3×10⁶ x − 4.5×10¹⁴ t) V/m (where x, t and other values have S.I. units). The dielectric constant of the medium is:
explanation: The wave speed is v = ω/k = 4.5×10¹⁴/3×10⁶ = 1.5×10⁸ m/s, so the refractive index n = c/v = 2. For a non-magnetic medium, κ = n² = 4.

subject: Physics
question_text: A parallel beam of light travelling in air (refractive index 1.0) is incident on a convex spherical glass surface of radius of curvature 50 cm. Refractive index of glass is 1.5. The rays converge to a point at a distance x cm from the centre of curvature of the spherical surface. The value of x is ___ cm.
explanation: Using the spherical refracting surface formula μ₂/v − μ₁/u = (μ₂ − μ₁)/R with u = ∞: 1.5/v = 0.5/50, giving v = 150 cm from the pole. Measured from the centre of curvature, x = 150 − 50 = 100 cm.

subject: Physics
question_text: A circular disc has radius R₁ and thickness T₁. Another circular disc made of the same material has radius R₂ and thickness T₂. If the moments of inertia of both the discs are the same and R₁/R₂ = 2, then T₁/T₂ = 1/α. The value of α is:
explanation: I = (1/2)mR² = (1/2)πρR⁴T. With I₁ = I₂, R₁⁴T₁ = R₂⁴T₂, so T₁/T₂ = (R₂/R₁)⁴ = (1/2)⁴ = 1/16, giving α = 16.

subject: Physics
question_text: Inductance of a coil with 10⁴ turns is 10 mH and it is connected to a DC source of 10 V with internal resistance 10 Ω. The energy density in the inductor when the current reaches (1/e) of its maximum value is απ × (1/e²) J/m³. The value of α is: (μ₀ = 4π×10⁻⁷ Tm/A)
explanation: I_max = 10/10 = 1 A, so the required current is (1/e) A. With B = μ₀nI and u = B²/2μ₀, the energy density = (μ₀n²/2)(1/e²) = 20π(1/e²) J/m³, so α = 20.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Consider the transition metal ions Mn³⁺, Cr³⁺, Fe³⁺ and Co³⁺, and all form low spin octahedral complexes. The correct decreasing order of unpaired electrons in their respective d-orbitals of the complexes is:
explanation: For low spin octahedral complexes: Cr³⁺ (d³) has 3 unpaired, Mn³⁺ (d⁴) has 2, Fe³⁺ (d⁵) has 1 and Co³⁺ (d⁶) has 0. Hence the order is Cr³⁺ > Mn³⁺ > Fe³⁺ > Co³⁺.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: The formal charges on the atoms marked as (1) to (4) in the Lewis representation of the HNO₃ molecule respectively are:
explanation: Formal charge = valence electrons − non-bonding electrons − bonding electrons/2. In the Lewis structure of HNO₃ the marked atoms carry formal charges 0, +1, 0 and −1 respectively.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Phenol on treatment with CHCl₃/aq. KOH under refluxing condition, followed by acidification, produces p-hydroxybenzaldehyde as the major product and o-hydroxybenzaldehyde as the minor product. Statement II: The mixture of p-hydroxybenzaldehyde and o-hydroxybenzaldehyde can be easily separated through steam distillation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.2: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.4: Statement I is false but Statement II is true

explanation: The Reimer–Tiemann reaction gives o-hydroxybenzaldehyde as the major product, so Statement I is false. The ortho isomer is steam volatile while the para isomer is not, so they are separated by steam distillation — Statement II is true.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: The energy required by electrons, present in the first Bohr orbit of hydrogen atom, to be excited to the second Bohr orbit is ___ J mol⁻¹. Given: R_H = 2.18×10⁻¹¹ ergs.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A p-block element E and hydrogen form a binary cation (EH₄)⁺, while EH₃ on treatment with K₂HgI₄ in alkaline medium gives a precipitate of basic mercury(II) amido-iodide. Given below are first ionisation enthalpy values (kJ mol⁻¹) for the first element each from groups 13, 14, 15 and 16. Identify the correct first ionisation enthalpy value for element E:
explanation: The cation is NH₄⁺ and NH₃ gives the brown precipitate with K₂HgI₄ (Nessler's reagent), so E is nitrogen, whose first ionisation enthalpy is 1402 kJ mol⁻¹.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: In the reaction, 2Al(s) + 6HCl(aq) → 2Al³⁺(aq) + 6Cl⁻(aq) + 3H₂(g):

options.1: 11.2 L H₂(g) at STP is produced for every mole of HCl consumed
options.2: 67.2 L H₂(g) at STP is produced for every mole of Al that reacts
options.3: 12 L HCl(aq) is consumed for every 6 L H₂(g) produced
options.4: 33.6 L H₂(g) is produced regardless of temperature and pressure for every mole of Al that reacts

explanation: From the equation, 3 mol H₂ are produced per 6 mol HCl, i.e. 0.5 mol H₂ = 11.2 L at STP per mole of HCl consumed. Statement (1) is therefore correct.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Consider a solution of CO₂(g) dissolved in water in a closed container. Which one of the following plots correctly represents the variation of log(partial pressure of CO₂ in vapour phase above water) [y-axis] with log(mole fraction of CO₂ in water) [x-axis] at 25°C?
explanation: By Henry's law, p = K_H·x, so log p = log K_H + log x — a straight line of slope 1 with intercept log K_H, which is the correct plot.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A first row transition metal M does not liberate H₂ gas from dilute HCl. 1 mol of aqueous solution of MSO₄ is treated with excess of aqueous KCN and then H₂S(g) is passed through the solution. The amount of MS (metal sulphide) formed from the above reaction is ___ mol.
explanation: The metal is copper (it does not liberate H₂ from dilute HCl). CuSO₄ with excess KCN forms the very stable [Cu(CN)₄]³⁻ complex, so H₂S does not precipitate CuS — 0 mol of MS is formed.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: The correct order of reactivity of CH₃Br in methanol with the following nucleophiles is: F⁻, I⁻, C₂H₅O⁻ and C₆H₅O⁻:
explanation: In a protic solvent (methanol), nucleophilicity follows basicity: I⁻ > C₂H₅O⁻ > C₆H₅O⁻ > F⁻ (fluoride is strongly solvated and least nucleophilic).

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Match the LIST-I with LIST-II (Thermodynamic process — Magnitude in kJ): A. Work done in reversible isothermal expansion of 2 mol of ideal gas from 2 dm³ to 20 dm³ at 300 K → I. 4; B. Work done in irreversible isothermal expansion of 1 mol ideal gas from 1 m³ to 3 m³ at 300 K against a constant pressure of 3 kPa → II. 11.5; C. Change in internal energy for adiabatic expansion of 1 mol ideal gas with change of temperature = 320 K and Cᵥ = 3R/2 → III. 6; D. Change in enthalpy at constant pressure of 1 mole ideal gas with change of temperature 337 K and C_p = 5R/2 → IV. 7. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: A: W = −nRT ln(V₂/V₁) = −2×8.314×300×2.303 = −11.5 kJ (II). B: W = −PΔV = −3×2 = −6 kJ (III). C: ΔU = nCᵥΔT = 1×(3R/2)×320 = 4 kJ (I). D: ΔH = nC_pΔT = 1×(5R/2)×337 = 7 kJ (IV). So A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Benzene is nitrated to give nitrobenzene, which on further treatment with CH₃COCl/AlCl₃ will give the product [shown]. Statement II: −NO₂ group is a meta-directing and deactivating group. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.1: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
options.2: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
options.3: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct

explanation: Nitrobenzene is so strongly deactivated that it does not undergo Friedel–Crafts acylation, so Statement I is incorrect. The −NO₂ group is meta-directing and deactivating — Statement II is correct.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A → products (First order reaction). Three sets of experiments were performed for a reaction under similar experimental conditions: Run 1 = 100 mL of 10 M solution of reactant A; Run 2 = 200 mL of 10 M solution of reactant A; Run 3 = 100 mL of 10 M solution of reactant A + 100 mL of H₂O added. The correct variation of rate of reaction is:
explanation: For a first order reaction, rate = k[A]. Runs 1 and 2 both have [A] = 10 M, so the same rate; Run 3 is diluted to 5 M, so its rate is lower. Hence Run 3 < Run 1 = Run 2.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Match the LIST-I with LIST-II (Reagents involving carbonyl compound — Name of reaction): A. NH₂−NH₂, KOH → I. Tollen's Test; B. Ag(NH₃)₂OH → II. Clemmensen Reduction; C. Aq. CuSO₄, Sodium Potassium tartarate, KOH → III. Wolff-Kishner Reduction; D. Zn−Hg, HCl → IV. Fehling's Test. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: NH₂−NH₂/KOH is the Wolff–Kishner reduction (III), Ag(NH₃)₂OH is Tollen's reagent (I), Fehling's solution uses CuSO₄ with sodium potassium tartarate in alkali (IV), and Zn–Hg/HCl is the Clemmensen reduction (II).

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The halogen that makes the longest bond with hydrogen in HX, has the smallest covalent radius in its group. Statement II: A group 15 element's hydride EH₃ has the lowest boiling point among corresponding hydrides of other group 15 elements. The maximum covalency of that element E is 4. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.1: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.2: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.4: Statement I is true but Statement II is false

explanation: HI has the longest H–X bond but iodine has the largest covalent radius, so Statement I is false. The hydride with the lowest boiling point is PH₃, and phosphorus has a maximum covalency of 6 (not 4), so Statement II is also false.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Sucrose is dextrorotatory. However, sucrose upon hydrolysis gives a solution having a mixture of products. This solution shows laevorotation. Statement II: Hydrolysis of sucrose gives glucose and fructose. Since the laevorotation of glucose is more than the dextrorotation of fructose, the resulting solution becomes laevorotatory. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.1: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.2: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are false
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are true

explanation: Sucrose is dextrorotatory and its hydrolysis gives a laevorotatory mixture (invert sugar), so Statement I is true. The reason is that fructose is strongly laevorotatory (more than glucose's dextrorotation), so the reason in Statement II is false.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: A is a neutral organic compound (M.F.: C₈H₉ON). On treatment with aqueous Br₂/HO⁻, A forms a compound B which is soluble in dilute acid. B on treatment with aqueous NaNO₂/HCl (0–5°C) produces a compound C which on treatment with CuCN/NaCN produces D. Hydrolysis of D produces E which is also obtainable from the hydrolysis of A. E on treatment with acidified KMnO₄ produces F. F contains two different types of hydrogen atoms. The structure of A is:
explanation: A is p-methylbenzamide (p-CH₃−C₆H₄−CONH₂). Br₂/HO⁻ converts it to the amine (Hofmann) which is soluble in dilute acid; diazotisation, Sandmeyer reaction with CuCN, hydrolysis and KMnO₄ oxidation give a dicarboxylic acid having two types of hydrogen atoms, confirming the para-methyl benzamide structure.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: The correct order of the rate of reaction of the following reactants with nucleophile by S_N1 mechanism is: (Given: Structures I and II are rigid):
explanation: S_N1 rate depends on carbocation stability. Structures I and II are bridged and cannot form a stable carbocation (Bredt's rule), with II having more +I effect than I; structure III gives the most stable carbocation and IV the least. So the order is IV < I < II < III.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Two p-block elements X and Y form fluorides of the type EF₃. The fluoride compound XF₃ is a Lewis acid and YF₃ is a Lewis base. The hybridizations of the central atoms of XF₃ and YF₃ respectively are:
explanation: XF₃ = BF₃ is an electron-deficient Lewis acid with sp² hybridization; YF₃ = NF₃ has a lone pair on nitrogen (Lewis base) and is sp³ hybridized.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: As compared with chlorocyclohexane, which of the following statements correctly apply to chlorobenzene? A. The magnitude of negative charge is more on the chlorine atom. B. The C–Cl bond has partial double bond character. C. C–Cl bond is less polar. D. C–Cl bond is longer due to repulsion between delocalised electrons of the aromatic ring and lone pairs of electrons of chlorine. E. The C–Cl bond is formed using sp² hybridised orbital of carbon. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
explanation: In chlorobenzene the C–Cl bond has partial double-bond character (B), is less polar than in chlorocyclohexane (C), and is formed using an sp² hybridised carbon orbital (E). Hence B, C and E only.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The Henry's law constant K_H is constant with respect to variations in solution concentration over the range for which the solution is ideally dilute. Statement II: K_H does not differ for the same solute in different solvents. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.1: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.2: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.3: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.4: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

explanation: K_H is constant over the ideally dilute range (Statement I true). K_H depends on the nature of the gas and the solvent, so it does differ across different solvents (Statement II false).

subject: Chemistry
question_text: The cycloalkene X on bromination consumes one mole of bromine per mole of X and gives the product Y in which C : Br ratio is 3 : 1. The percentage of bromine in the product Y is ___ % (Nearest integer). Given: Molar mass in g mol⁻¹ H: 1, C: 12, O: 16, Br: 80.
explanation: With C : Br = 3 : 1, the dibromide product is C₆H₁₀Br₂ (M = 242). %Br = (160/242)×100 = 66.11% ≈ 66.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Consider the following electrochemical cell at 298 K: Pt|HSnO₂⁻(aq)|Sn(OH)₆²⁻(aq)|OH⁻(aq)|Bi₂O₃(s)|Bi(s). If the reaction quotient at a given time is 10⁶, then the cell EMF (E_cell) is ___ × 10⁻¹ V (Nearest integer). Given the standard half-cell reduction potential as E°(Bi₂O₃/Bi, OH⁻) = −0.44 V and E°(Sn(OH)₆²⁻/HSnO₂⁻, OH⁻) = −0.90 V.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: The temperature at which the rate constants of the given below two gaseous reactions become equal is ___ K (Nearest integer). X → Y, k₁ = 10⁶ e^(−30000/T); P → Q, k₂ = 10⁴ e^(−24000/T). Given: ln 10 = 2.303.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Sodium fusion extract of an organic compound Y with CHCl₃ and chlorine water gives violet colour to the CHCl₃ layer. 0.15 g of Y gave 0.12 g of the silver halide precipitate in Carius method. Percentage of halogen in the compound Y is ___ (Nearest integer). Given: C: 12, H: 1, Cl: 35.5, Br: 80, I: 127.
explanation: The violet colour indicates iodine (NaI). %I = (At. wt. of I/At. wt. of AgI) × (mass of AgI/mass of compound) × 100 = (127/235) × (0.12/0.15) × 100 = 43.23% ≈ 43.

subject: Chemistry
question_text: Dissociation of a gas A₂ takes place according to the following chemical reaction. At equilibrium, the total pressure is 1 bar at 300 K. A₂(g) ⇌ 2A(g). The standard Gibbs energy of formation of the involved substances has been provided below: Substance ΔG_f°/kJ mol⁻¹: A₂ → −100.00; A → −50.832. The degree of dissociation of A₂(g) is given by (x × 10⁻²)^(1/2), where x = ___ (Nearest integer). [Given: R = 8 J mol⁻¹K⁻¹, log 2 = 0.3010, log 3 = 0.48. Assume degree of dissociation is not negligible.]
explanation: ΔG° = 2(−50.832) − (−100) = −1.664 kJ mol⁻¹. From ΔG° = −RT ln K_p, ln K_p = 0.693, so K_p = 2. With total pressure 1 bar, p_A = 2α/(1+α) and p_A₂ = (1−α)/(1+α), so K_p = 4α²/(1−α²) = 2, giving α = 1/√3 = (33.33×10⁻²)^(1/2), hence x = 33.
